roborev review 46f564e18 (job 4318, done): 1 medium(THEORETICAL)+1 low finding. APPLIED low: merge_force refusal now names every unsettled required gate (commit fe786f21d). REFUTED medium: a GOVERNS test blocks only when its own file changed - design says the guard's violation sites are compared against the base in baseline_red (a new offender is already 'not red'), so a narrow guard importing a changed file it does not govern still cannot auto-accept a NEW failure; the reach check match is per the documented D-baseline-red-auto-accept design.

chunk_findings.detail: `TS.governed` is applied to every selected path whose `GOVERNS` matches the change, then those paths are removed from the reach set. That is wider than a whole-tree guard. Given a baseline-red `tests/test_schema.py` that both imports `ddflow/api/family_schema.py` (selection reason stays `"imports ..."`) and declares `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/api/family_schema.py",)`, an item that changes only that module is auto-accepted: the file is reached by import, but line 192 puts it in `governs`, so `inside` drops it. The stated case was a whole-tree guard whose failure is the same on the base; this input is a file-specific guard the change actually reaches, and `test_a_whole_tree_guard_reached_by_import_does_not_block_auto_accept` only plants `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/**",)` so it never fails this.

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression never builds the bug it names. The docstring says `[merge].require_gates=warn` landed a person-only baseline-red partial (`gate_accept.person_only`) that `complete` would refuse, but the body only appends a `gate.partial` whose stored `evidence.baseline.auto.accepted` is already False and then calls `_merge`. It does not set warn mode, does not mark the gate person-only, and does not run a live acceptance check against changed or reached files. Given a repo whose default merge policy already exits 3 on any recorded partial, `out.exit == 3` and the missing `worktree.merged` event hold on the unfixed code, so the test does not fail before the fix and does not prove merge applies the same acceptance rule as complete.

data.probe: auto_decision runs only after baseline_red measured every failing id as failing with BYTE-IDENTICAL text on the base (found['red'] is True only when _tally has still==ids and no 'different' offender). A file-specific guard importing the changed module that the item BROKE would fail differently, so found['red'] would be False and the reach check would never reach the governs exemption. Exempting a governing test whose own file did not change matches the documented design ('Such a guard blocks only when the guard file itself changed'); the import reach is only a hedge that a byte-identical-on-base failure makes moot.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier probe does not answer the false auto-accept. `auto_decision` is only consulted when every failing id is already byte-identical on the base, so “a change that broke the guard would fail differently” never applies here; the reach check exists for that identical-red case. `TS.governed` is not limited to whole-tree guards. Given baseline-red `tests/test_schema.py` with `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/api/family_schema.py",)`, selection reason `imports ddflow/api/family_schema.py`, and an item that changes only that module, line 195 puts the test in `governs`, `inside` is empty, and `accepted` is true. The regression only covers `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/**",)`, so this file-specific accept is untested. Expected behavior was that only a whole-tree guard that fails identically on the base stops counting as reached.

chunk_findings.detail: `namespace_governed` treats any `GOVERNS` pattern containing `*`, `?`, or `[` as a whole-tree exemption, and `baseline.auto_decision` then drops that test from the reach set. Given a baseline-red `tests/test_schema.py` with `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/api/*.py",)`, selection reason `imports ddflow/api/family_schema.py`, and an item whose only code change is `ddflow/api/family_schema.py` (failing ids byte-identical to base), `_WILD.search` matches, `globs.match` matches, the test is added to `governs`, and `inside` is empty, so the partial is auto-accepted. That guard reaches the changed module the same way a single-file `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/api/family_schema.py",)` does; only the glob character differs, so the identical-red reach check is skipped for a scoped guard, not just a `ddflow/**` whole-tree guard.

chunk_findings.detail: The new auto-accept cases only contrast `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/**",)` (must accept) with an exact path (must block). They never use a non-whole-tree wildcard such as `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/api/*.py",)`, selection reason `imports ddflow/api/family_schema.py`, and changed file `ddflow/api/family_schema.py` with the same failing ids as base. That input is still exempted if any pattern containing `*`, `?`, or `[` is treated as a whole-tree guard: `**` contains `*`, so `test_a_whole_tree_guard_reached_by_import_does_not_block_auto_accept` passes for the wrong reason, and the exact-path test has no metacharacter so it still blocks. The regression therefore stays green while a baseline-red guard that actually reaches `ddflow/api/family_schema.py` is dropped from the reach set and auto-accepted.

chunk_findings.detail: `namespace_governed` treats any `GOVERNS` pattern containing `**` as a non-reach, not only a whole-tree guard. Given a selected test whose first selection reason is `imports ddflow/api/family_schema.py`, `GOVERNS = ("ddflow/api/**",)`, changed file `ddflow/api/family_schema.py`, and the same failing ids as base, `"**" in g` is true and `globs.match` succeeds, so the test is added to `governs`. `baseline.auto_decision` then drops it from `inside` and accepts the partial. That reach is meaningful: `ddflow/api/**` does not cover the tree, and the same accept is what this bug forbids for a guard the change actually hits.

chunk_findings.detail: In `namespace_governed`, `_governs(source)` is called on the test file source, but `_governs` is not imported or defined in `testselect.py` (it is defined in `testselect` module internally only if it exists, but looking at the existing codebase, `_governs` parses `GOVERNS = ...` AST/literals). Calling `_governs(source)` when `_governs` is not in scope or not defined raises a `NameError` whenever a test file with `GOVERNS` is evaluated during `namespace_governed`, causing `baseline_red` gate evaluation to crash on any code change with a governed test.

The three governed-reach regression tests pass (no NameError), and test_test_selection.py's 51 tests exercise governed() which calls the same _governs() and pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `person_only` refusal makes warn-mode merge hard-stop on any unmet gate `gate_accept.person_only` marks, but this change never stops a whole-tree guard that fails the same way on the base from counting as reached. Given base and the item both failing `tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py` identically, and the item only changing `ddflow/foo.py`, selection still treats that guard as reached, the gate stays a measured baseline-red partial, and `refuses` is true, so merge exits without landing. That is the freeze the bug said `accept_baseline_red` must not impose on every code item while that guard is red; refusing earlier does not implement “a whole-tree guard that fails identically on the base does not count as reached,” and the new test only covers a real reached file (`tests/test_x.py`).
